title: Model cards and review
goals: Write a model card whose claims match evidence
Separate intended use from unsupported use
Review a card for missing evaluation details

prerequisite.prompt: What should remain visible after an evaluation?
prerequisite.answer: Data provenance, model version, full results, limitations and decision history.

vocabulary: A concise structured account of a model and its limits
The purpose and conditions the evidence supports
A purpose for which the model is not supported
The current state of checks and unresolved issues

blocks.text: A model card helps another person understand what was built and what evidence exists. It is a record, not a certificate of safety. Link statements to saved data and run records. Use unknown or not evaluated where evidence is absent instead of filling gaps with optimistic language.

Use fictional classroom data throughout this investigation. Keep the task, units, reference labels and data split visible as you reason. Earlier weeks supplied the model-building process; this week examines model cards and review.

Example card: classroom parcel classifier v 1; purpose: compare toy classification methods on fictional clear/blocked labels. Training 40, validation 20, test 12 with separate record groups. Frozen test TN 7 FP 1 FN 2 TP 2, blocked positive: accuracy 9/12, precision 2/3, recall 2/4. Always-clear baseline scores 8/12. No real parcel or student decision is supported.

Before continuing, underline the decision rule and circle the evidence that supports the conclusion. Explain the example to a partner without replacing the counts or conditions with a stronger claim. Keep the distinction between an observed result and a proposed next step.

blocks.title: Model cards and review at a glance
blocks.caption: The model card should name feature availability, preprocessing fitted on training, model settings, reference-label rules and test date. Include subgroup coverage if evaluated; otherwise say it was not assessed. Describe relevant failure examples without exposing personal information.

blocks.label: Verify the worked accuracy, precision and recall. Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

blocks.text: A peer reviewer traces one headline number back to the saved predictions, checks denominators and looks for mismatches between intended use and evidence. Record requested changes and whether each was resolved. A card must be updated when its model, data or intended use changes.

Do not claim a synthetic classroom dataset represents every school or age group. Missing calibration, subgroup or shift evidence must remain explicit. A useful card may conclude that the model should stay a classroom demonstration.

blocks.label: What should change in a card after a threshold revision?

workbook.title: Draft a purpose
workbook.prompt: Write an intended-use and non-use statement for the worked card.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Intended: compare toy classifiers on the documented fictional task. Not supported: real parcel handling, student assessment or decisions outside the evaluated setup.

workbook.title: Check arithmetic
workbook.prompt: Verify the worked accuracy, precision and recall.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: TN 7 TP 2 give 9/12 accuracy; TP 2/(TP 2+FP 1)=2/3 precision; TP 2/(TP 2+FN 2)=2/4 recall.

workbook.title: Find missing evidence
workbook.prompt: A card says fair and reliable but provides only accuracy. Request three additions.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Request full error counts and denominators, relevant subgroup coverage/results, data provenance and limits; remove unsupported fairness/reliability claims.

workbook.title: Apply independently
workbook.prompt: Review this card: model v 2, 90 percent accurate, works for every school. No dataset size, split or baseline is given. Write a correction request with a bounded replacement claim.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Request evaluated counts, split history, reference labels, baseline, errors and supported use. Replace the universal claim with: performance scope is not established from the supplied evidence; the reported 90 percent cannot yet be audited.

workbook.title: Maintain the record
workbook.prompt: What should change in a card after a threshold revision?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Record a new version, threshold, reason, affected evaluations and review status; retain prior results and distinguish new independent evidence from reused development data.

teacher.background: Teach two 45-minute sessions. This week focuses on model cards and review. Model the worked example first, collect the new W 4 case independently before feedback, and use the fresh retry to check transfer. Award credit for traceable reasoning and bounded claims, including justified uncertainty.
materials: Paper, pencils and a calculator for fractions
The fictional examples and a blank evidence table
Saved classroom project records for critique; no personal student dataset required
sessions: Use the prerequisite question: What should remain visible after an evaluation? Check the explanation before proceeding.
Read the opening and model the worked evidence. Ask students to identify model card in context.
Complete W 1 and W 2 with support: draft a purpose; check arithmetic. Require the evidence, not only the final response.
Read the visual row by row. Collect the guided explanation and compare reasoning in pairs. Connect each conclusion to the stated evidence.
Retrieve the distinction between model card and intended use. Invite a counterexample to an overconfident claim.
Discuss the application and complete W 3: A card says fair and reliable but provides only accuracy. Request three additions.
Collect W4 independently before giving hints. Assess these outcomes: Write a model card whose claims match evidence; Separate intended use from unsupported use. Record any support used.
Use W 5 and the exit response to assess limits. Give targeted feedback, then the fresh retry. Save evidence of independent understanding.

misconceptions: Ask for the relevant counts, units, procedure or saved record. For this week: Intended: compare toy classifiers on the documented fictional task. Not supported: real parcel handling, student assessment or decisions outside the evaluated setup.
A stronger claim makes a stronger project

The new case can be copied from the example

The independent task changes the evidence. Require a fresh explanation: Request evaluated counts, split history, reference labels, baseline, errors and supported use. Replace the universal claim with: performance scope is not established from the supplied evidence; the reported 90 percent cannot yet be audited.
teacher.assessment: For independent W 4, require: Request evaluated counts, split history, reference labels, baseline, errors and supported use. Replace the universal claim with: performance scope is not established from the supplied evidence; the reported 90 percent cannot yet be audited. Fresh retry: a card lists test accuracy 18/20 but omits positive-class recall and intended use. Ask for full matrix, class definition and bounded use; do not infer recall from accuracy. Mark each criterion as independent, supported or not yet demonstrated. Reassess the reasoning after feedback; do not replace the first attempt silently.
teacher.support: Provide a blank evidence table and allow a verbal explanation before writing. Highlight the given conditions without supplying the W 4 conclusion. Use model card and intended use in full sentences. Extension: alter one condition in the worked example and explain which conclusion changes and which remains supported.
teacher.next: Next week: Capstone data and requirements. Carry forward the saved evidence and the distinction between development choices and justified claims.
